sections.title: Full crew lifecycle flow
sections.what: Walks one crew from creation through invitation, joining, outsider blocking, code rotation and leaving, checking the result at each step.
sections.why: Covers the whole sharing and privacy path in one run, so breaks between steps are caught.
sections.watch_out: Each step depends on the one before, so one early failure hides the later checks.

summary: Browser test of the whole crew lifecycle: create a crew, invite a friend by link, join, rotate the invite code, leave, and check outsiders see nothing.
purpose: Confirms that crews, the group feature, work and are private to their members.
why: Crews group users together, so both the sharing flow and the privacy rules need an end-to-end check.
how: It creates three users and three separate browser sessions. The owner creates a crew and reads the invite link. The friend follows the link, is sent to sign in, and lands in the crew with the owner and themselves listed. An outsider asking for the crew page gets a 404. The owner then generates a new code, and the old link shows an invalid message. Finally the friend leaves and the owner's member list no longer shows them.
inputs: Three new users, the crew name, and the invite link shown on the page.
outputs: Pass or fail for each step. No data is kept after the run.
risks: The test relies on the invite code format and the exact wording of the invalid-link message, so copy changes will break it.
debug: Check each step in order. If the friend cannot join, check the invite link and sign-in redirect. If the outsider sees the crew, the access rule is broken.
